title: Searching for life on another planet
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: describes a place or habitat that is suitable for something to live
an area with a particular feature
describes possibly having qualities or abilities to do something
dismiss the possibility or idea of something
controlled by or is the most significant element of
an expression we use to wish for hope or luck

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 这里是BBC英语教学的6 Minute English。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Becca. Neil, do you believe that life exists away from planet Earth?
sentences.zh: 我是Neil。我是Becca。Neil，你相信地球之外存在生命吗？

sentences.en: Well, I'm not sure about the kind of little green men that you see in science fiction movies, but also, I think we cannot be alone in the universe.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不确定是不是你在科幻电影里看到的那种小绿人，但我也觉得我们在宇宙中不可能孤单。

sentences.en: What about you, Becca? What do you think?
sentences.zh: 你呢，Becca？你觉得呢？

sentences.en: I agree, I think that maybe life does exist beyond our planet, but maybe not as we see in alien movies.
sentences.zh: 我同意，我认为生命可能存在于我们的星球之外，但也许不像我们在外星人电影中看到的那样。

sentences.en: Well, in this episode, we'll be learning from science and space experts about whether the conditions for life exist on a planet 40 light years away.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在本期节目中，我们将向科学和太空专家了解40光年外的一个行星是否存在生命存在的条件。

sentences.en: Yes, and as usual, you can find a transcript for this episode, along with all the vocabulary and a worksheet, on our website bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 是的，和往常一样，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到本期节目的文稿、所有词汇以及练习页。

sentences.en: OK, a quiz question for you, Becca. How long would it take to drive a car to the Sun at 100km an hour?
sentences.zh: 好的，Becca，给你出一个问答题。以每小时100公里的速度开车去太阳需要多长时间？

sentences.en: Is it: a) 70 years, b) 170 years, or c) 1,700 years?
Well, Neil, the Sun seems very far away so I’ll go for c) 1,700 years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，Neil，太阳似乎非常遥远，所以我选 c) 1,700年。

sentences.en: I hope you have enough petrol for that. Well, we’ll find out the answer to the question later.
sentences.zh: 我希望你带够了汽油。好吧，我们稍后会揭晓答案。

sentences.en: Now, though, some science and space experts are excited about a planet in a different solar system from our own.
sentences.zh: 不过现在，一些科学和太空专家对我们自己太阳系之外的一颗行星感到兴奋。

sentences.en: Science journalist, Caroline Steele, talks about this discovery on the BBC World Service programme What in the World.
sentences.zh: 科学记者Caroline Steele在BBC世界服务节目 What in the World 上谈论了这一发现。

sentences.en: So, scientists have been looking at an exoplanet.
sentences.zh: 所以，科学家们一直在观察一颗系外行星。

sentences.en: So, that's a planet that exists in a solar system that isn't our own, called TRAPPIST-1e, um, and it's a rocky planet like Earth.
sentences.zh: 也就是一颗存在于不属于我们自己的太阳系中的行星，名叫 TRAPPIST-1e，嗯，它是一颗像地球一样的岩石行星。

sentences.en: It's a similar size to Earth, and it exists in the habitable zone around its sun, and its sun is called TRAPPIST-1.
sentences.zh: 它的大小与地球相似，存在于其太阳周围的宜居带中，它的太阳被称为 TRAPPIST-1。

sentences.en: Caroline explains that scientists have discovered that the planet, TRAPPIST-1e, exists in the habitable zone around its sun.
sentences.zh: Caroline解释说，科学家们发现行星 TRAPPIST-1e 存在于其太阳周围的宜居带中。

sentences.en: The adjective habitable describes a place or habitat that is suitable for something to live.
sentences.zh: 形容词 habitable 描述了一个适合某物居住的地方或栖息地。

sentences.en: Yes, and a zone is an area with a particular feature.
sentences.zh: 是的，zone 是指具有特定特征的区域。

sentences.en: For example, people who live in earthquake zones have to be prepared for danger.
sentences.zh: 例如，生活在地震带的人们必须对危险做好准备。

sentences.en: So, a habitable zone is an area where something could live.
sentences.zh: 所以，宜居带就是可能存在生命居住的区域。

sentences.en: Caroline goes on to explain why they think TRAPPIST-1e may be habitable.
sentences.zh: Caroline 接着解释了他们认为 TRAPPIST-1e 可能宜居的原因。

sentences.en: Scientists have been looking at the potential atmosphere around TRAPPIST-1e and they've ruled out that it's really full of hydrogen or carbon dioxide, which is a great thing because they're greenhouse gases, which would make the planet really hot.
sentences.zh: 科学家们一直在研究 TRAPPIST-1e 周围的潜在大气层，他们已经排除了它充满氢气或二氧化碳的可能性，这太棒了，因为它们是温室气体，会让行星变得非常热。

sentences.en: And there are some small clues that it might be a nitrogen- dominated atmosphere, which, again, is another sort of clue that there could be life there.
sentences.zh: 并且有一些小线索表明它可能是以氮气为主的大气层，这也是那里可能存在生命的另一种线索。

sentences.en: Caroline Steele says that scientists are looking at the potential atmosphere around TRAPPIST-1e.
sentences.zh: Caroline Steele 表示，科学家们正在研究 TRAPPIST-1e 周围的潜在大气层。

sentences.en: That is, that they want to find out if the atmosphere is capable or likely to become able to host life.
sentences.zh: 也就是他们想弄清楚大气层是否有能力或可能变得有能力孕育生命。

sentences.en: If something has potential, it already has the qualities or abilities to do something.
sentences.zh: 如果某事物具有 potential，它就已经具备做某事的品质或能力。

sentences.en: The adjective potential has a similar meaning but refers to future capability.
sentences.zh: 形容词 potential 具有相似的含义，但指的是未来的能力。

sentences.en: Exactly. We could say the data has potential in that it shows signs of helping the research.
sentences.zh: 没错。我们可以说这些数据具有潜力，因为它显示出有助于研究的迹象。

sentences.en: But when we talk about potential data, we're referring to data that could help us with future research.
sentences.zh: 但当我们谈论潜在数据时，我们指的是可能帮助我们进行未来研究的数据。

sentences.en: She also mentions how scientists have ruled out that TRAPPIST-1e is full of hydrogen or carbon dioxide.
sentences.zh: 她还提到科学家是如何排除 TRAPPIST-1e 充满氢气或二氧化碳的可能性的。

sentences.en: The phrasal verb rule out means to dismiss the possibility or idea of something.
sentences.zh: 短语动词 rule out 意为排除某种可能性或想法。

sentences.en: Scientists have found that TRAPPIST-1e is not full of those greenhouse gases, they’ve ruled it out.
sentences.zh: 科学家发现 TRAPPIST-1e 并没有充满这些温室气体，他们已经排除了这种可能。

sentences.en: Indeed. And Caroline goes on to say how the atmosphere of TRAPPIST-1e is dominated by nitrogen.
sentences.zh: 的确。Caroline 接着说到 TRAPPIST-1e 的大气层是如何被氮气主导的。

sentences.en: If something is dominated by something else, it is controlled by it or is the most significant element of it.
sentences.zh: 如果某事物被其他事物 dominated，它就会被其控制或成为其中最重要的元素。

sentences.en: TRAPPIST-1e is full of nitrogen, which is exciting because nitrogen is a sign of life and habitability.
sentences.zh: TRAPPIST-1e 充满了氮气，这令人兴奋，因为氮气是生命和宜居性的迹象。

sentences.en: So, what if nitrogen is actually found on this planet?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果在该行星上真的发现了氮气会怎么样呢？

sentences.en: Caroline Steele has more. My guess is what we'll do is try and see what other gases are in the atmosphere and use models to work out how warm the planet could be and whether or not it's a temperature that basically could support life, or maybe it's too hot or too cold, but fingers crossed it has nitrogen.
sentences.zh: Caroline Steele 还有更多说法。我的猜测是，我们将要做的是尝试看看大气层中还有哪些气体，并使用模型来计算出该行星会有多温暖，以及它是否是基本上可以支持生命的温度，或者也许它太热或太冷，但祈祷它有氮气吧。

sentences.en: There's enough of it to keep the planet a decent temperature.
sentences.zh: 有足够多的氮气来保持行星处于合适的温度。

sentences.en: And then that's one step closer to finding life.
sentences.zh: 然后这就离发现生命更近了一步。

sentences.en: Caroline guesses that scientists will focus on the planet’s temperature and whether it could support life.
sentences.zh: Caroline 猜测科学家将专注于该行星的温度以及它是否能支持生命。

sentences.en: She uses the expression fingers crossed to express hope for a positive outcome.
sentences.zh: 她使用了短语 fingers crossed 来表达对积极结果的希望。

sentences.en: Yes. We often make the physical gesture of crossing our fingers for good luck.
sentences.zh: 是的。我们经常做出交叉手指的身体手势来祈求好运。

sentences.en: We do. That reminds me Neil, the answer to your question!
sentences.zh: 我们确实这么做。这让我想起了 Neil，你那个问题的答案！

sentences.en: Fingers crossed that I answered correctly.
sentences.zh: 祈祷我回答正确吧。

sentences.en: I see what you've done there, Becca. Yes, I asked you how long it would take to drive to the Sun at 100km an hour, and you answered c) 1,700 years.
sentences.zh: 我明白你刚才的意图了，Becca。是的，我问你以每小时100公里的速度开车去太阳需要多长时间，你回答了 c) 1,700年。

sentences.en: Well, the Sun is very far away, but the answer was b) only 170 years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，太阳非常遥远，但答案是 b) 只有170年。

sentences.en: Oh well, that’s still longer than my lifetime!
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧，那仍然比我的寿命要长！

sentences.en: Now let’s have a recap of the language we've learnt in this episode, starting with habitable, which describes a place or habitat that is suitable for something to live.
sentences.zh: 现在让我们回顾一下我们在本节目中学到的语言，从 habitable 开始，它描述了适合某物居住的地方或栖息地。

sentences.en: A zone is an area with a particular feature.
sentences.zh: zone 是指具有特定特征的区域。

sentences.en: Potential describes possibly having qualities or abilities to do something.
sentences.zh: Potential 描述可能具备做某事的品质或能力。

sentences.en: The phrasal verb rule out means to dismiss the possibility or idea of something.
sentences.zh: 短语动词 rule out 意为排除某种可能性或想法。

sentences.en: We also had dominated. If something is dominated by something else, it is controlled by it or is the most significant element of it.
sentences.zh: 我们还学了 dominated。如果某事物被其他事物主导，它就被其控制或成为其中最重要的元素。

sentences.en: And finally, the expression fingers crossed is used to wish for hope or luck.
sentences.zh: 最后，短语 fingers crossed 用于表达希望或祈求好运。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but head over to our website, bbclearningenglish.com, for a quiz and worksheet for this episode.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟时间又到了，但请访问我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com，获取本期节目的测验和练习页。

sentences.en: See you soon. Goodbye for now. Bye!
sentences.zh: 回头见。先这样，拜拜！
